About Your Privacy

We process your data to deliver content or advertisements and measure the delivery of such content or advertisements to extract insights about our website. We share this information with our partners on the basis of consent and legitimate interest. You may exercise your right to consent or object to a legitimate interest, based on a specific purpose below or at a partner level in the link under each purpose. These choices will be signaled to our vendors participating in the Transparency and Consent Framework and saved in a cookie on your device called “fides_consent” for a maximum duration of 12 months.

Below, you will find a list of the purposes and special features for which your data is being processed. You may exercise your rights for specific purposes, based on consent or legitimate interest, using the toggles below.
Purposes
Essential
On

This website uses essential cookies and services to enable core website functionality and provide a seamless user experience. These cookies and services are used to facilitate features such as navigation, remembering user references, and ensuring website security.

Functional Cookies
On

These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Audience Measurement
On

We use audience measurement cookies in order to carry out aggregated traffic measurement and generate performance statistics essential for the proper functioning of the site and the provision of its content (for example to measure performance, to detect navigation problems, to optimization technical performance or ergonomics, to estimate server power needed and to analyse content performance). The use of these cookies is strictly limited to measuring the site's audience. These cookies do not allow the tracking of navigation on other websites and the data collected is not combined or shared with third parties. You can refuse the use of this cookie by switching off the slider to the right.

Targeted Advertising
On

These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

Performance Cookies
On

These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Social Media Cookies
On

These cookies are set by a range of social media services that we have added to the site to enable you to share our content with your friends and networks. They are capable of tracking your browser across other sites and building up a profile of your interests. This may impact the content and messages you see on other websites you visit. If you do not allow these cookies you may not be able to use or see these sharing tools.

Store and/or access information on a device
On
IAB TCF

Cookies, device or similar online identifiers (e.g. login-based identifiers, randomly assigned identifiers, network based identifiers) together with other information (e.g. browser type and information, language, screen size, supported technologies etc.) can be stored or read on your device to recognise it each time it connects to an app or to a website, for one or several of the purposes presented here.

Most purposes explained in this notice rely on the storage or accessing of information from your device when you use an app or visit a website. For example, a vendor or publisher might need to store a cookie on your device during your first visit on a website, to be able to recognise your device during your next visits (by accessing this cookie each time).

A car manufacturer wants to promote its electric vehicles to environmentally conscious users living in the city after office hours. The advertising is presented on a page with related content (such as an article on climate change actions) after 6:30 p.m. to users whose non-precise location suggests that they are in an urban zone.

A large producer of watercolour paints wants to carry out an online advertising campaign for its latest watercolour range, diversifying its audience to reach as many amateur and professional artists as possible and avoiding showing the ad next to mismatched content (for instance, articles about how to paint your house). The number of times that the ad has been presented to you is detected and limited, to avoid presenting it too often.

Create profiles for personalised advertising

IAB TCF

Information about your activity on this service (such as forms you submit, content you look at) can be stored and combined with other information about you (for example, information from your previous activity on this service and other websites or apps) or similar users. This is then used to build or improve a profile about you (that might include possible interests and personal aspects). Your profile can be used (also later) to present advertising that appears more relevant based on your possible interests by this and other entities.

If you read several articles about the best bike accessories to buy, this information could be used to create a profile about your interest in bike accessories. Such a profile may be used or improved later on, on the same or a different website or app to present you with advertising for a particular bike accessory brand. If you also look at a configurator for a vehicle on a luxury car manufacturer website, this information could be combined with your interest in bikes to refine your profile and make an assumption that you are interested in luxury cycling gear.

An apparel company wishes to promote its new line of high-end baby clothes. It gets in touch with an agency that has a network of clients with high income customers (such as high-end supermarkets) and asks the agency to create profiles of young parents or couples who can be assumed to be wealthy and to have a new child, so that these can later be used to present advertising within partner apps based on those profiles.

    10 hydrating sheet masks to give your skin a pre-party moisture boost

    Fifteen minutes of skincare before several hours of questionable decisions
    By Siya Bhambwani
    25 October 2026
    Representative image. Photographed by Tenzing Dakpa
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 6:42
    Instaread

    So, you spent 40 minutes on your makeup only to discover that your foundation has settled into dry patches you didn't even know existed. You can blame the weather, the air conditioning or the fact that you've been rather inconsistent with your skincare lately, but none of that is particularly helpful when you're getting ready to go out. Hydrating sheet masks, however, might be.

    Most sheet masks are soaked in serums containing humectants such as hyaluronic acid and glycerin, which help increase water content in the skin's outermost layers. Depending on the formula, you might also find ceramides to support the skin barrier, centella asiatica to soothe irritation or niacinamide to help improve uneven-looking skin over time. The immediate benefit is that skin that looks a little plumper, feels less tight and provides a smoother starting point for makeup.

    The trick is knowing what your skin actually needs. A hydrogel mask designed for extended wear is a different proposition from a serum-soaked sheet mask you can use while doing your hair. And if your skin is easily irritated, introducing unfamiliar active ingredients an hour before a party may not be the most inspired decision.

    Below, 10 hydrating sheet masks worth considering before your next evening out:

    COSRX Advanced Snail Mucin Glass Glow Hydrogel Mask

    COSRX has built much of its reputation around snail mucin and this hydrogel mask contains 25% snail secretion filtrate alongside five forms of hyaluronic acid, ceramides and panthenol. The combination addresses dehydration and moisture-barrier support, while niacinamide and gluconolactone add a brightening and mild exfoliating element.

    Why we love it: The combination of humectants and barrier-supporting lipids makes sense for dry, dull-looking skin, although anyone sensitive to exfoliating acids should take note of the gluconolactone.

    Justhuman Peace Mask

    Centella asiatica, allantoin and sodium hyaluronate help soothe and hydrate, while niacinamide, glutathione and vitamin E contribute antioxidant and skin-conditioning benefits. The formula also contains rose extract and sodium DNA. Designed to be worn for 15–20 minutes, it's one of the more practical options for a quick pre-makeup routine.

    Why we love it: It combines hydration with ingredients aimed at calming visible irritation, without requiring several hours of wear.

    Beauty of Joseon Centella Asiatica Calming Mask

    Centella asiatica appears high on the ingredient list, accompanied by niacinamide, panthenol, hyaluronic acid and botanical extracts including mugwort, green tea and ginseng. Together, they make this a hydration-focused formula with an emphasis on soothing skin that feels uncomfortable or looks flushed. The 15–20-minute application time is also convenient, particularly after a day spent outdoors or in air-conditioned spaces.

    Why we love it: A good choice when redness and dehydration are greater concerns than brightness. It also contains chamomile flower oil for extra soothing.

    Innisfree Hyaluronic Acid Active Mask

    Hyaluronic acid is a humectant, meaning it binds water and helps increase hydration in the skin's outer layers, making it useful when dehydration leaves fine lines looking more pronounced or makeup catches on rough areas. The appeal is straightforward: a temporary moisture boost without making exfoliation or intensive brightening the focus of your pre-party skincare.

    Why we love it: The added hydration can temporarily plump up the skin's surface, making fine dehydration lines less noticeable and helping makeup sit more evenly without adding another complicated step to your routine.

    Biodance Hydro Cera-nol Real Deep Mask

    Biodance's Hydro Cera-nol complex combines ceramides, panthenol and multiple forms of hyaluronic acid, targeting both hydration and the skin's moisture barrier. Ceramides are particularly useful because they form part of the lipids naturally found between skin cells, helping limit moisture loss. The formula also contains glycerin, betaine and allantoin. Its hydrogel format is intended for extended wear, becoming more transparent over several hours, so this is better suited to a slower skincare evening than a last-minute makeup session.

    Why we love it: The emphasis on barrier-supporting ingredients makes it especially relevant for skin that feels persistently dry or tight, rather than simply lacking radiance.

    The Face Shop Vita-Toning Collagen Face Mask

    This two-piece hydrogel mask contains 10 forms of hyaluronic acid, niacinamide, glutathione and a vitamin complex, with plant-derived collagen included for its skin-conditioning properties. While the collagen is unlikely to rebuild the skin's own collagen, the humectants can temporarily improve hydration and make skin appear smoother. The mask gradually becomes more transparent during its recommended 20–40-minute wear time.

    Why we love it: A useful option for skin that looks dehydrated and uneven, particularly when you want a hydration-focused treatment without committing to an overnight mask.

    VT Cosmetics PDRN Hydrogel Mask

    PDRN has become a much-discussed skincare ingredient, but it is worth distinguishing topical formulas from the injectable treatments that helped popularise it. VT Cosmetics uses ginseng-derived PDRN, alongside panthenol, squalane, niacinamide and lactobacillus ferment. The hydrogel can be worn for 20–40 minutes or left on longer for a more extended treatment.

    Why we love it: The combination of squalane, panthenol and glycerin gives the formula a credible hydration story, even without relying on the more ambitious claims surrounding PDRN.

    SK-II Facial Treatment Mask

    SK-II's Facial Treatment Mask takes a relatively pared-back approach, centring its formula on Pitera, the brand's proprietary galactomyces ferment filtrate. The fermentation-derived ingredient contains a mixture of naturally occurring compounds, including amino acids, and is used for its skin-conditioning properties.

    Why we love it: A relatively simple ingredient list and short application time make this an interesting luxury option for those who prefer their pre-party skincare without an extensive routine.

    d'Alba Piedmont White Truffle Nourishing Treatment Mask

    White truffle extract is the star ingredient here, while glycerin, betaine and several forms of hyaluronic acid do much of the practical moisturising work. The formula also includes centella asiatica, allantoin, bifida ferment lysate and saccharide isomerate, a humectant that helps bind moisture to the skin.

    Why we love it: An option for skin that needs additional moisture, although the extensive botanical blend makes it one to try well before an important event if you're prone to irritation.

    Dr.Jart+ Cryo Rubber Soothing Face Mask

    Unlike a traditional serum-soaked sheet, Dr.Jart+'so Rubber mask is a two-step treatment. A concentrated ampoule is applied first, followed by a flexible, cooling rubber mask that sits over the skin. The soothing version contains allantoin, an ingredient used to help calm and protect skin, alongside peptides. The cooling sensation is a particularly appealing feature when skin feels warm or looks flushed, although any reduction in redness should be understood as temporary rather than a treatment for its underlying cause.

    Why we love it: The cooling format offers something different from the usual sheet mask, making it worth considering when skin feels overheated or uncomfortable before an evening out.
